significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that sign-flipping the objective on subliminal data produces an oppositely signed behavioral effect whose magnitude is approximately predicted by ordinary transfer strength, alongside the form-(ii) mechanism that the student steering vector becomes "anti-aligned (negative cosine) with the teacher's." This would fix expected outcomes across multiple trait strengths and explain when the gradient-alignment account in Cloud et al.'s "Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data" supports inversion, establishing both a behavioral sign-symmetry phenomenon and a causal optimization-to-representation mechanism rather than merely another transferred trait. The branches are distinguishable despite some softness in "roughly symmetric": failure of anti-trait installation or of the signed coupling would rule out sign reversibility as a general consequence of the linear-gradient account, although it would not refute subliminal transfer itself. In the topic-substitution self-check, the generic goal of extending subliminal-learning research would not earn this score; the claim-specific signed law, anti-alignment mechanism, and informative negative branch place it above the topic median.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the proposed "practical, label-free inoculation" implemented through a "sign-flipped objective," supplemented by ordinary positive-transfer strength as a predictor of the anti-trait magnitude. This is ex ante because it changes a student during training before the undesirable behavior is deployed, giving model trainers and safety practitioners an action window rather than merely explaining failures afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted symmetry relation still predicts a negative sign and approximately matched magnitude, although the substantive scope remains limited to settings where subliminal transfer occurs—especially matched-base models—and the claim does not establish universal transfer across arbitrary architectures or training regimes. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: subliminal learning alone supplies no reversible training knob or forecast, whereas the quoted inoculation and symmetry claims could alter how downstream practitioners train or gate models.
